correctness.rationale: Testing the normalized monomials up to 2m-1 forces the radial rule sum alpha_j x_j^k=k!, with alpha_j=q_j exp(-x_j)/C and x_j the distinct squared radii. The square of the polynomial vanishing on all nodes excludes fewer than m radii by positivity of e^{-x}dx, also for adjustable weights. At exactly m nodes orthogonality of the monic node polynomial gives an invertible integer-moment Gram system, so the nodes are algebraic; the first m moments give invertible Vandermonde equations and algebraic masses. For each pair of distinct nodes, exp(x_i-x_j)=q_i alpha_j/(q_j alpha_i) would be algebraic, contradicting Hermite–Lindemann. A common external positive factor cancels and angles do not enter the necessity. The monic orthogonal polynomial has m simple positive roots by the sign-change argument. Interpolation modulo that polynomial gives Gaussian exactness, and integrating squared Lagrange polynomials proves positivity of the masses. Regular 2m-gons remove all off-diagonal terms; weights alpha_j exp(x_j)/(2m) give unit diagonals. Thus the positive-weight minimum is m, while m+1 is a lower bound, not an existence assertion, for equal external weights. The restriction m>=2 is essential: at n=1 a single radius with x=1 and two antipodal samples gives equality.
